title: Face Charge Scale for the Returned-Payment Fee — Benefit Overpayment Accounts
content:
The returned-payment fee owed on Benefit Overpayment Accounts for a repayment the bank returned unpaid carries a face charge, and the fee's face charge follows the amount on the return entry being charged. The return entry being charged is the most recent return entry booked on the overpayment.

## Scale

| Amount on the return entry being charged | Face charge |
|---|---|
| Above USD 300.00 (the upper face-amount threshold) | USD 40.00, the upper-tier face charge |
| Above USD 50.00 (the lower face-amount threshold) and up to USD 300.00 | USD 30.00, the middle-tier face charge |
| At or below USD 50.00 | The classification's returned-payment fee, which the payment terms list at USD 25.00 for every classification |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical amounts)

| Amount returned | Tier | Face charge |
|---|---|---|
| USD 300.01 | Above the upper threshold | USD 40.00 |
| USD 300.00 | Up to the upper threshold | USD 30.00 |
| USD 50.01 | Above the lower threshold | USD 30.00 |
| USD 50.00 | At the lower threshold | USD 25.00 |
| USD 12.00 | Below the lower threshold | USD 25.00 |

## Points of judgement

- The amount compared is the amount on the return entry being charged, not the overpayment balance and not the amount of an earlier return.
- Each threshold belongs to the lower tier: exactly USD 300.00 takes the middle-tier charge, and exactly USD 50.00 takes the classification's returned-payment fee.
